name: Performance Rulebook
summary: Fast loading, smooth interaction and stable layout, measured with Core Web Vitals.
check: Lighthouse on mobile for each page type; PageSpeed Insights field data once live.
Check bundle sizes against the budget in CI.

rules.title: Compress images
rules.text: Modern formats (AVIF/WebP), correct dimensions, `srcset` and `sizes`, explicit `width` and `height` to prevent layout shift.

rules.title: Lazy loading
rules.text: Images, iframes and heavy sections below the fold load lazily (`loading="lazy"`); nothing in the first viewport does.

rules.title: Core Web Vitals
rules.text: Good LCP (under 2.5 s), INP (under 200 ms) and CLS (under 0.1).

rules.title: Code splitting
rules.text: Load only the JavaScript the current page needs.

rules.title: Minify JS and CSS
rules.text: Production builds minify JavaScript and CSS; any modern bundler does this when configured for production.

rules.title: Defer non-critical scripts
rules.text: Analytics, chat and embeds load with `defer`, `async` or after interaction.

rules.title: Remove unused dependencies
rules.text: Uninstall packages nothing imports, and replace heavy libraries used for one small function with a few lines of code or a lighter alternative.

rules.title: Unnecessary re-renders
rules.text: In React and similar: keep state local, memoise expensive parts, avoid new objects in props on every render.

rules.title: Debounce input handlers
rules.text: Search-as-you-type waits about 250–300 ms after the last keystroke.

rules.title: Paginate or virtualise long lists
rules.text: Lists of more than about 50–100 items are paginated, loaded in batches, or virtualised so only visible rows are rendered.

rules.title: Use a CDN
rules.text: Static files are served from a CDN close to visitors.

rules.title: Cache API responses
rules.text: API responses are cached on the client and the server wherever the data allows.

rules.title: Server-side caching
rules.text: Rendered pages or fragments are cached on the server or at the edge.

rules.title: Cache expensive queries
rules.text: Expensive queries (statistics, rankings) are cached and refreshed on a schedule instead of computed per request.

rules.title: Index the database
rules.text: Columns used for lookups, filters and sorting have database indexes.

rules.title: N+1 queries
rules.text: Load related data in one query (JOIN, eager loading), not one query per item.

rules.title: Compress API payloads
rules.text: Return only needed fields; enable gzip or brotli.

rules.title: Database connection pooling
rules.text: Servers reuse a pool of database connections instead of opening a new one per request; serverless functions use the provider's pooler.

rules.title: Load balancing
rules.text: When traffic needs more than one server, a load balancer spreads it and health checks remove broken instances.

rules.title: Lighthouse audit
rules.text: Run Lighthouse before launch on every page type, on mobile, and fix what it flags.

rules.title: Heavy visuals stay light
rules.text: WebGL, video and large animations render only while visible, cap pixel ratio and frame rate, and have a static fallback for weak devices and reduced motion.

rules.title: Prioritise the LCP image
rules.text: The largest image above the fold is a real `` in the HTML with `fetchpriority="high"`, never lazy-loaded.

rules.title: Preconnect to critical origins
rules.text: `<link rel="preconnect">` for the one or two third-party origins needed above the fold (fonts, image CDN).

rules.title: Long cache for hashed assets
rules.text: Fingerprinted files get `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; HTML is revalidated.

rules.title: Critical CSS first
rules.text: CSS needed for the first screen is inlined or loaded first; the rest does not block rendering.

rules.title: A performance budget
rules.text: Agree limits (for example under about 170 KB of compressed JavaScript for the first load, LCP under 2.5 s on a mid-range phone) and check them in CI (`GH-11`).

rules.title: Keep the back/forward cache working
rules.text: No `unload` handlers and no `Cache-Control: no-store` on normal pages, so Back is instant.

rules.title: Break up long tasks
rules.text: JavaScript work over about 50 ms is split up or moved to a worker so input stays responsive (INP under 200 ms).

rules.title: Skip off-screen rendering
rules.text: `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size` on long pages with heavy sections below the fold.

rules.title: Client-rendering static pages
rules.text: Do not ship a JavaScript app to render content that never changes per visitor. Pre-render it.

rules.title: Autoplaying hero video on mobile data
rules.text: Large background videos do not autoplay on small screens or with `prefers-reduced-data`; show a poster image.

rules.title: Too many third-party scripts
rules.text: Every tag, widget and pixel costs performance and privacy. Remove what nobody looks at; load the rest after interaction or consent.

rules.title: Huge DOM
rules.text: Avoid pages with thousands of nodes. Paginate, virtualise or simplify markup (about 1,500 nodes is a warning sign).

rules.title: Render 3D on demand
rules.text: A WebGL scene on a page draws only when something changes: render on demand (`frameloop="demand"` in React Three Fiber) and request a frame from scroll, pointer and running animations. Cap the pixel ratio at 2 (1 is enough below 768 px for heavy scenes), load the 3D code as its own chunk and prefetch it as soon as the page starts. Draw the shadow map by hand (`shadowMap.autoUpdate = false`) while the scene or the light changes, and keep drawing it for about 24 frames after the last change, because parts updated a frame late would otherwise freeze a stale shadow.
